Let \(C=[10]\setminus B=\{6,7,8,9,10\}\).  
Every \(S\in\mathcal X\) at distance \(k\) from \(B\) is uniquely
\[
S=(B\setminus I)\cup J,\qquad I\subset B,\ J\subset C,\ |I|=|J|=k.
\]
Thus the \(k\)-th layer is the tensor product of the permutation spaces on \(k\)-subsets of two \(5\)-sets.

On \(k\)-subsets of a \(5\)-set, the Johnson adjacency eigenvalue on the \(r\)-th component is
\[
\alpha_k(r)=(k-r)(5-k-r)-r,
\]
where \(r=0,1,2\), with multiplicities
\[
m_0=1,\qquad m_1=4,\qquad m_2=5.
\]
This component appears exactly for \(r\le k\le 5-r\). Also the incidence map from \(k\)-subsets to \((k+1)\)-subsets has squared singular value
\[
\beta_k(r)^2=(k+1-r)(5-k-r)
\]
on the \(r\)-th component.

Therefore \(A\) splits into tridiagonal blocks indexed by pairs \((r,s)\in\{0,1,2\}^2\). For fixed \((r,s)\), the allowed levels are
\[
k=\max(r,s),\dots,5-\max(r,s),
\]
with diagonal entries
\[
26+k-\alpha_k(r)-\alpha_k(s),
\]
and off-diagonal squared entries
\[
\beta_k(r)^2\beta_k(s)^2.
\]
Each such block determinant is raised to power \(m_rm_s\).

Computing the small tridiagonal determinants gives:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
(r,s)&\det T_{r,s}&m_rm_s\\ \hline
(0,0)&28681627&1\\
(0,1),(1,0)&250272&4\\
(0,2),(2,0)&591&5\\
(1,1)&622127&16\\
(1,2),(2,1)&866&20\\
(2,2)&1055&25
\end{array}
\]
Hence
\[
\det A
=
28681627\cdot 250272^8\cdot 591^{10}\cdot 622127^{16}\cdot 866^{40}\cdot 1055^{25}.
\]
Factoring,
\[
28681627=13\cdot73\cdot30223,
\]
\[
250272=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot11\cdot79,\quad
591=3\cdot197,\quad
622127=11\cdot23\cdot2459,
\]
\[
866=2\cdot433,\quad
1055=5\cdot211.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{2^{80}3^{26}5^{25}11^{24}13\cdot23^{16}\cdot73\cdot79^8\cdot197^{10}\cdot211^{25}\cdot433^{40}\cdot2459^{16}\cdot30223}.
\]
